speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of AIDS and are experiencing decreased vision and floaters in your right eye. To narrow this down, how long have these symptoms been present, and is there any pain or redness in the eye?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of Kaposi's sarcoma and recent fungal esophagitis, have you noticed any new skin lesions or oral ulcers, and did you have any recent fevers or night sweats?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, HIV viral load, and CD4 count.
REQUEST IMAGES: Fundus photography of the right eye.

speaker: Doctor
text: With a CD4 count of only 36/mm³, your immune system is severely compromised, which strongly suggests an opportunistic infection like Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. The fundus photos I ordered should clarify this; can you confirm if you have had any recent fevers or weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) Retinitis. The low CD4 count of 36/mm³ combined with painless floaters and vision loss in an immunocompromised host is classic for this opportunistic infection. Please confirm the fundus images show "pizza-pie" retinal hemorrhages and necrosis to finalize the diagnosis.
